subject: maths
title: Place Value to 100: Tens and Ones, Partitioning and Comparing
seo_title: Year 2 Place Value Worksheets: Tens and Ones, Numbers to 100 in Words
standard_text: Recognise the place value of each digit in a two-digit number (tens, ones); identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations, including the number line; compare and order numbers from 0 up to 100; use <, > and = signs; read and write numbers to at least 100 in numerals and in words; use place value and number facts to solve problems.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 place value maths worksheets for the National Curriculum: tens and ones with blocks and straws, partitioning (47 = 40 + 7), numbers to 100 in words, comparing with <, > and =, and number lines. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A 2-digit number is tens and ones. The 4 in 47 is worth 40.
key_sub: 47 = 40 + 7, and it is also 3 tens and 17 ones. To compare numbers, look at the tens first, then the ones.
body_html:
Tens and ones

A 2-digit number has a tens digit and a ones digit. The place tells you what the digit is worth. 10 ones make 1 ten.

Partition

Split a number into tens and ones: 47 = 40 + 7. You can also swap 1 ten for 10 ones: 47 is 3 tens and 17 ones, because 30 + 17 = 47.

Partition

Split 63 into tens and ones.

63 is 6 tens and 3 ones. 6 tens = 60.

Answer: 63 = 60 + 3

Numbers in words

NumeralWordsTens and ones
14fourteen1 ten and 4 ones
40forty4 tens and 0 ones
64sixty-four6 tens and 4 ones
90ninety9 tens and 0 ones
100one hundred10 tens

“Teen” numbers have 1 ten. “Ty” numbers have lots of tens. Use a hyphen in sixty-four.

Compare with < > =

Look at the tens first. If the tens are the same, look at the ones.

Compare

52 ☐ 49

Tens: 5 tens > 4 tens. Stop here. The 9 ones do not matter.

Answer: 52 > 49

< means “is less than”. > means “is greater than”. = means “is the same as”. The open side faces the bigger number.

Estimate on a number line

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing forty-seven as 74 or 407Tens first, then ones: 47
Saying the 4 in 47 is worth 4It is in the tens place: 40
Comparing the ones first (49 > 52)Compare the tens first: 52 > 49
Mixing up fourteen and fortyFourteen is 14, forty is 40
Spelling fourty or nintyforty, ninety

faq.q: What place value should a Year 2 child know?
faq.a: Year 2 children work with numbers up to 100. They know the tens and ones in a 2-digit number, read and write numbers in numerals and words, compare and order numbers with <, > and =, and find numbers on a number line.

faq.q: What does partitioning mean in Year 2 maths?
faq.a: Partitioning means splitting a number into parts, usually tens and ones: 47 = 40 + 7. Children also learn other ways, such as 47 = 30 + 17.

faq.q: Why does my child write 407 for forty-seven?
faq.a: They write each part they hear: 40 and then 7. Show 4 tens and 7 ones with blocks or straws, then write the tens digit and the ones digit: 47.

faq.q: How do you teach < and > signs in Year 2?
faq.a: Compare the tens first, then the ones, and say “is less than” or “is greater than”. The open side of the sign always faces the bigger number, as in 52 > 49.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20. Then add 5 ones: 20 + 5 = 25. Each rod is 10, not 1.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30. Then add 8 ones: 30 + 8 = 38.

items.q: How many straws are there?
items.e: A bundle is 10 straws. Count the bundles in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. Then add 6 ones: 40 + 6 = 46.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: Count the rods: 3 tens. Count the small cubes: 6 ones. The number is 36.

items.q: How many tens are in 58?
items.e: 58 is 5 tens and 8 ones. There are 5 tens.

items.q: How many ones are in 36?
items.e: 36 is 3 tens and 6 ones. There are 6 ones.
A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. There are no ones, so write 0 in the ones place: 60.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 6 is in the tens place. It is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: What is the 4 in 47 worth?
items.e: In 47 the 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 40. 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones.

items.q: How many straws are there?
items.e: A bundle is 10 straws. Count the bundles in tens: 10. Then add 9 ones: 10 + 9 = 19.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Then add 2 ones: 50 + 2 = 52.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 8 is in the ones place. It is worth 8 ones = 8.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: Count the rods: 5 tens. Count the small cubes: 9 ones. The number is 59.

items.q: How many tens are in 90?
items.e: 90 is 9 tens and 0 ones. There are 9 tens.

items.q: What is the 5 in 85 worth?
items.e: In 85 the 5 is in the ones place, so it is worth 5.

items.q: How many straws are there?
items.e: A bundle is 10 straws. Count the bundles in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80. Then add 3 ones: 80 + 3 = 83.
A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. Then add 4 ones: 70 + 4 = 74.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 9 is in the tens place. It is worth 9 tens = 90. The digit is 9, but its value is 90.

items.q: Which number has 3 ones and 8 tens?
items.e: Write the tens first, then the ones. 8 tens and 3 ones make 83.

items.q: What is the 7 in 72 worth?
items.e: In 72 the 7 is in the tens place, so it is worth 70. 72 is 7 tens and 2 ones.

sets.title: Partition numbers into tens and ones

items.q: What is 60 + 4?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. 4 is 4 ones. 6 tens and 4 ones = 64. Not 604.
47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. 4 tens = 40. So 47 = 40 + 7.
63 is 6 tens and 3 ones. 6 tens = 60, not 6. So 63 = 60 + 3.

items.q: Which shows 72 split into tens and ones?
items.e: 72 is 7 tens and 2 ones. 7 tens = 70. So 72 = 70 + 2.

items.q: What is 7 + 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens and 7 is 7 ones. Tens come first: 57. The order you add them does not matter.
85 is 8 tens and 5 ones. 85 = 80 + 5.

items.q: Which shows 38 split into tens and ones?
items.e: 38 is 3 tens and 8 ones. 3 tens = 30. So 38 = 30 + 8.

items.q: What is 4 tens and 9 ones?

items.e: 29 is 2 tens and 9 ones. 2 tens = 20. So 20 + 9 = 29.

items.q: Which shows 56 split into tens and ones?
items.e: 56 is 5 tens and 6 ones. 5 tens = 50. So 56 = 50 + 6.

items.q: What is 8 tens and 0 ones?
items.e: 8 tens = 80. There are 0 ones, so the number is 80.

items.q: There are 3 tens and 17 ones. What number is it?
items.e: 3 tens = 30. 17 ones = 1 ten and 7 ones. So 30 + 17 = 47.
26 can be 1 ten and 16 ones. 10 + 16 = 26. (6 is wrong: 10 + 6 = 16.)

items.q: 47 is 3 tens and ☐ ones.
items.e: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. Take 1 ten and make it 10 ones. Now there are 3 tens and 10 + 7 = 17 ones. Check: 30 + 17 = 47.

items.q: What is 2 tens and 15 ones?
items.e: 2 tens = 20. 15 ones = 1 ten and 5 ones. So 20 + 15 = 35.

items.q: Which is another way to make 52?
items.e: 52 is 5 tens and 2 ones. Take 1 ten and make it 10 ones: 4 tens and 12 ones. 40 + 12 = 52.

items.q: 64 is 5 tens and ☐ ones.
items.e: 64 is 6 tens and 4 ones. Take 1 ten and make it 10 ones: 5 tens and 14 ones. Check: 50 + 14 = 64.

items.q: What is 5 tens and 12 ones?
items.e: 5 tens = 50. 12 ones = 1 ten and 2 ones. So 50 + 12 = 62.

items.q: Which is the same as 36?
items.e: 36 is 3 tens and 6 ones. Take 1 ten and make it 10 ones: 2 tens and 16 ones. 20 + 16 = 36.

items.q: Which is NOT the same as 45?
items.e: 3 tens and 5 ones is 30 + 5 = 35, not 45. The others all make 45: 40 + 5 and 30 + 15.

sets.title: Numbers to 100 in numerals and words

items.q: Write fourteen in numerals.
items.e: Fourteen is 1 ten and 4 ones, so write 14. Do not mix it up with forty, which is 40.

items.q: Write forty in numerals.
items.e: Forty is 4 tens and 0 ones, so write 40. Numbers ending in “ty” are tens. Fourteen is 14.

items.q: How do you write 64 in words?
items.e: 64 is 6 tens and 4 ones. Say the tens, then the ones, with a hyphen: sixty-four.

items.q: How do you write 14 in words?
items.e: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. Numbers from 13 to 19 end in “teen”: fourteen. Spell it four + teen. Forty is 40.

items.q: How many tens are in seventy-two?
items.e: Seventy-two is 72: 7 tens and 2 ones. There are 7 tens.

items.q: Write sixty-three in numerals.
items.e: Sixty-three is 6 tens and 3 ones, so write 63. Do not write 603: a 2-digit number has only 2 digits.

items.q: How do you write 40 in words?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Tens end in “ty”: forty. Forty has no “u”, but four and fourteen do.

items.q: Which shows the number in words?
items.e: 2 rods and 7 cubes: 2 tens and 7 ones = 27. In words: twenty-seven.

items.q: Write eighteen in numerals.
items.e: Eighteen is 1 ten and 8 ones, so write 18. Do not mix it up with eighty, which is 80.

items.q: How do you write 17 in words?
items.e: 17 is 1 ten and 7 ones. Numbers from 13 to 19 end in “teen”: seventeen.

items.q: Write ninety-one in numerals.
items.e: Ninety-one is 9 tens and 1 one, so write 91. Do not write 901: a 2-digit number has only 2 digits.

items.q: How do you write 82 in words?
items.e: 82 is 8 tens and 2 ones. Say the tens, then the ones, with a hyphen: eighty-two.

items.q: How many ones are in forty-eight?
items.e: Forty-eight is 48: 4 tens and 8 ones. There are 8 ones.

items.q: Write seventy in numerals.
items.e: Seventy is 7 tens and 0 ones, so write 70. Numbers ending in “ty” are tens. Seventeen is 17.

items.q: How do you write 90 in words?
items.e: 90 is 9 tens. Tens end in “ty”: ninety. Ninety keeps the “e” from nine.
5 rods and no cubes: 5 tens = 50. In words: fifty. Fifteen is 15.

items.q: Write thirty-five in numerals.
items.e: Thirty-five is 3 tens and 5 ones, so write 35. Do not write 305: a 2-digit number has only 2 digits.

items.q: How do you write 55 in words?
items.e: 55 is 5 tens and 5 ones. Say the tens, then the ones, with a hyphen: fifty-five.

items.q: Write fifty-nine in numerals.
items.e: Fifty-nine is 5 tens and 9 ones, so write 59. Do not write 509: a 2-digit number has only 2 digits.

items.q: How do you write 73 in words?
items.e: 73 is 7 tens and 3 ones. Say the tens, then the ones, with a hyphen: seventy-three.

sets.title: Compare, order and estimate with <, > and =

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 74 has 7 tens and 47 has 4 tens. So 74 > 47. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 52 has 5 tens and 49 has 4 tens. So 52 > 49. Do not look at the ones first: 9 ones is less than 1 ten. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. Count in tens from 0: 10, 20, 30.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tens first, then the ones. In order: 29, 45, 68, 71. The greatest is 71. 29 has the biggest ones digit, but only 2 tens.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 83 has 8 tens and 38 has 3 tens. So 83 > 38. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

items.q: Which number is between 30 and 40?
items.e: Numbers between 30 and 40 have 3 tens: 31, 32, … 39. 34 has 3 tens, so it fits.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. Count in tens from 0: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the tens first, then the ones. In order: 35, 39, 50, 53. The smallest is 35.

items.q: Put 56, 65, 46 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones. From smallest to greatest: 46, 56, 65.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens first. 61 has 6 tens and 16 has 1 ten. So 61 > 16. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each mark is 10. The arrow is halfway between 40 and 50. Halfway is 45.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare the tens first, then the ones. In order: 80, 89, 90, 98. The greatest is 98.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 30 + 6 is 3 tens and 6 ones, which is 36. Both sides are the same, so use =.

items.q: Put 73, 37, 70 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones. From greatest to smallest: 73, 70, 37.

items.q: Which number is between 60 and 70?
items.e: Numbers between 60 and 70 have 6 tens: 61, 62, … 69. 67 has 6 tens, so it fits.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: The arrow is halfway between 0 and 50, so it is about 25. 75 is halfway between 50 and 100.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare the tens first, then the ones. In order: 12, 19, 21, 91. The smallest is 12. 19 and 12 both have 1 ten. 2 ones < 9 ones.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Fourteen is 14 (1 ten). Forty is 40 (4 tens). 14 < 40.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 1. Count on from 45: 46, 47. The arrow shows 47.

items.q: Put 18, 81, 80 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the ones. From smallest to greatest: 18, 80, 81.

items.q: Pencils come in packs of 10. Amelia has 3 packs and 4 more pencils. How many pencils does she have?
Zara thinks of a number. It has 8 tens and 5 ones. What is her number?
Use the digits 3 and 8 once each. What is the biggest 2-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the bigger digit in the tens place: 8 tens and 3 ones = 83. You cannot use 8 twice.

items.q: George has 53 stickers. He fills as many sheets of 10 as he can. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: 53 is 5 tens and 3 ones. 5 sheets use 50. 3 stickers are left over.

items.q: Evie counts her toy cars. She has 3 tens and 0 ones. How many toy cars does she have?
items.e: 3 tens = 30. There are 0 ones, so the number is 30.

items.q: Arjun thinks of a number between 40 and 50. It has 6 ones. What is his number?
items.e: Between 40 and 50 means 4 tens. 4 tens and 6 ones = 46.

items.q: Oliver has 2 tens and 13 ones in cubes. How many cubes is that?
items.e: 2 tens = 20. 13 ones = 1 ten and 3 ones. 20 + 13 = 33.

items.q: A teacher has 100 pencils. She puts them in pots of 10. How many pots does she fill?
Harry gets on the number 46 bus. What is the 4 worth?
items.e: The 4 is in the tens place. It is worth 4 tens = 40.

items.q: Maya writes 47 = 4 + 7. That is wrong. Which is right?
items.e: The 4 in 47 is 4 tens, so it is worth 40. 47 = 40 + 7. (4 + 7 is only 11.)

items.q: Noah keeps marbles in bags of 10. He has 6 bags and 2 more marbles. How many marbles does he have?
A shop has 7 bags of 10 apples and 9 loose apples. How many apples is that?
Use the digits 5 and 2 once each. What is the smallest 2-digit number you can make?
items.e: Put the smaller digit in the tens place: 2 tens and 5 ones = 25.

items.q: Class 1 has 31 children. Class 2 has 28 children. Which is true?
items.e: Look at the tens. 31 has 3 tens. 28 has 2 tens. So 28 < 31. Class 1 has more children.

items.q: Freya writes seventy-one on her card. Which number does she write?
items.e: Seventy-one is 7 tens and 1 one: 71. Seventeen is 17.

items.q: Isla has 47 stickers. She puts them on sheets of 10. How many full sheets can she make?
items.e: 47 is 4 tens and 7 ones. She can fill 4 sheets of 10.

items.q: Kai runs a 100 m race. The arrow shows where he is. How far has he run?
items.e: Each mark is 10 m. Count in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70. He has run 70 m.

items.q: Ruby needs 60 beads. Beads come on strings of 10. How many strings does she need?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. Each string is 1 ten. She needs 6 strings.

items.q: Biscuits come in packs of 10. The class needs 50 biscuits. How many packs do they need?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Each pack is 1 ten. They need 5 packs.

items.q: Four children play a game. Jack scores 39, Poppy scores 52, Leo scores 48 and Grace scores 25. Who scores the most?
items.e: Look at the tens. 52 has 5 tens. The others have fewer tens. Poppy scores the most. Jack has 9 ones, but only 3 tens.
